title: 08/01 — Sensitivity detector rules (what enters a protected state, and how we know)
owner: P7 (injected). D2, ratified 2026-08-21: the detector is P7's, injected, and — until this catalogue is wired — unwritten. This file is the injected rule content, not a P7 module.
consumer: a caller-built classification pass, run per file version over P4 observations, P5 sensitivity-signal rows, and P6's activation output, injected into P7's classification path. No module under src/privacy/ may hold these rules, patterns, or label lists at module level; the caller loads this JSON and compiles the patterns (same discipline as catalogues 02-07).

what_a_fired_rule_emits.rule_id: this catalogue's id, carried in the section-8.2 structured explanation
what_a_fired_rule_emits.kind: the rule's kind (null for basis = safety_domain rules); carried in the structured explanation, never a new column — P7's ClassificationRecord has no kind field and this catalogue invents no P7 columns or event types
what_a_fired_rule_emits.basis: detector | safety_domain — two of P7's three basis values; `user` is never a catalogue rule
what_a_fired_rule_emits.protected: the rule's boolean; true engages the three section-8.4 prohibitions verbatim
what_a_fired_rule_emits.handling_class_ceiling: the most protective class this rule ALONE may justify; the detector proposes, P7 assigns the class and owns the vocabulary
what_a_fired_rule_emits.evidence_refs: observation_keys per the rule's evidence_refs_shape; non-empty whenever basis = detector (P7 SPEC Contract out section 2)

write_shape.homes: D2 (ratified 2026-08-21): P7's ClassificationRecord keyed (file_id, content_hash) is authoritative; files.sensitivity_state is its projection via P1's set_sensitivity_state. Nothing in this shape is storage-specific, so a fired rule writes through either home unchanged if D2 is ever revisited.

rules_preamble: **Absence of a classification is never Public/low.** That resolution is P7's (absence resolves to unreadable_unclassified). This catalogue only says what happens when a rule DOES fire and what evidence it cites.

**Every detector rule is a conjunction.** No rule fires on a bare pattern, a bare filename, a bare extension, or a bare gazetteer hit. The model is 00's course-code discipline: "BUSIB 4300 becomes a course fact only when the engine finds a course-code pattern together with academic context such as" the named context terms.

**Format is never a class.** `.pdf` is not medical; `.csv` is not a credential export. Extension and source_type appear below only as conjuncts, mirroring the never-alone invariant on file_kind_plausible (CONNECTION section 5).

**Grouping is never an input.** Rules fire per file version on that file's own observations, signals, and activation — never on group membership. This is why the detector still fires on isolated residual material: 00: "Rare but sensitive files such as passports, visas, and legal documents may be surfaced as protected records even when they do not meet a normal group-size threshold." A fired rule is what lets the gate deny cloud for a file P10 never placed (the Protected Records residual, 00 section 7.3).

**No numeric thresholds.** Every count is a named injected slot with no default. Digits inside pattern strings describe document formats (an MRZ line's alphabet, a code-grid shape), never a decision threshold.
**No regex reaches src/.** Patterns live here as data; a later caller compiles them.
**Word-boundary matching** for every label and term list, per 00: "It should use word-boundary matching rather than substring matching."

**P5's signals are consumed, never re-derived.** Email addresses, message content, and VCF values already carry P5's `potentially sensitive` signal rows (src/extractors/long_tail.py). Rules below key on those stored rows; no rule re-detects an email address.

**User revision outranks every rule.** 00: "The classification is itself evidence-backed and can be revised by the user." A user_confirmed reclassification supersedes any rule's output; negative feedback stores the observation keys the rule fired on so the same signal does not resurface the same false protection (P7 SPEC, Correction learning).

entries.name: Passport machine-readable zone

signals.source: an OCR text unit or extracted text unit (P4 text_units; observations span into it)
signals.pattern: two consecutive lines each matching ^[A-Z0-9<]{40,44}$ with the first beginning P[A-Z<]
signals.notes: ICAO 9303 TD3 shape; OCR noise motivates the tolerant length band in the pattern, which describes a document format, not a threshold

signals.source: P5 source_type image, or a PDF routed to OCR (text_layer_absent)
signals.notes: 00's protected example is 'a scanned passport'; the MRZ arriving via OCR of an image or scanned PDF is the realistic carrier

entries.fire_condition: both signals; no count slot — a well-formed MRZ line pair is singular evidence
never_alone: the word 'passport' anywhere — a novel, a travel checklist, a visa-requirements article
a run of '<' characters in a diff, ASCII art, or an HTML fragment
an image with no OCR text — absence of text is not evidence of anything
evidence_refs_shape: observation_key of each MRZ-line observation (OCR region location and context fields preserved)
observation_key of the routing/format observation that establishes the scanned carrier
false_positive_notes: A museum or news photograph that includes a legible passport MRZ would fire; that is the over-protective direction and the user can revise (00: the classification 'can be revised by the user').
A specimen passport image in a design mock-up fires; acceptable for the same reason.
A visa-requirements blog post never fires: prose contains the word, not the MRZ shape.

entries.ceiling_provenance_note: the class name itself — 'Highly sensitive or credential-bearing' — names credential-bearing material; this is the one ceiling a design phrase supports directly

signals.source: extracted text observations (E3 structured text)
signals.notes: the armor header of PEM-encoded (RFC 7468 textual encoding) or OpenSSH private keys; the header plus a base64 body is the material itself

signals.source: the same text unit
signals.pattern: at least one subsequent line of base64-alphabet text before an -----END marker
signals.notes: excludes a bare header pasted into prose

entries.fire_condition: both signals; filename conventions (id_rsa, id_ed25519, *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx) are supporting context only and never required or sufficient

Test fixtures in cloned repositories mostly never reach P5 — P3 excludes descendants of software project roots — so the repo-key false-positive class is largely pre-filtered.

Binary keystores (.p12/.pfx) without extractable text cannot fire this rule; they surface as unreadable/metadata-only and stay unclassified, which resolves to unreadable_unclassified at the gate — never to public.

Ordinary signed contracts without notarization do not fire this rule; they are left to legal-domain safety activation, because a rule broad enough to catch every contract would protect every signed permission slip.

entries.protected_note: 00 does not put correspondence in the immediate-protected five; this rule classifies without protecting, so the mode matrix (hybrid keeps sensitive files local) still applies. Whether correspondence should ALSO be protected is in NEEDS-JOSEPH.

signals.notes: conjunct only; the signal rows are the evidence

an email address found in a non-email document (P5 signals address values only in email zones; an address in a syllabus footer is contact info on a public document)
a newsletter — it fires (it is an email with content); the CEILING is what keeps a newsletter's classification proportionate, and user revision handles the rest

false_positive_notes: Mailing-list archives and newsletters classify as sensitive_personal-at-most despite being effectively public; the cost is a local-first bias for material the user can release, which is the designed default direction (00: "The default posture must therefore be local-first and data-minimizing.").

design_cites.quote: while treating addresses and message content as potentially sensitive

an email signature block inside a document

refused.refuses: any rule of the shape extension/source_type → handling class or protected state (.pdf → medical, .csv → credential export, .vcf without P5 signal rows)
refused.why: format is a routing signal, never meaning; file_kind_plausible is constitutionally never-alone (CONNECTION section 5, invariant 2), and the dispatch instruction 'padding detector rules is how you get .pdf → medical' is the failure this row guards. Every rule above uses carrier signals as conjuncts only.

refused.refuses: any rule firing on a filename alone ('passport.jpg', 'taxes 2025.pdf', 'id_rsa')
refused.why: 00: "the system should not infer a purpose from their filename alone" — stated for unreadable files and a fortiori for protection, where a filename-fired classification would be evidence_refs pointing at nothing but a name. Filenames appear above only as supporting context.

design_cites.quote: the system should not infer a purpose from their filename alone

refused.refuses: a detection gazetteer of protected characteristics (race, religion, orientation, union membership, and the rest)
refused.why: 00 does not ask the product to detect these in order to file them, and the overnight review already flagged that "a catalogue that enumerated them would be instructing the extractor to look for them". The question of whether to detect-to-protect or decline-to-model goes to NEEDS-JOSEPH; this catalogue does not fill the list.

design_cites.quote: a catalogue that enumerated them would be instructing the extractor to look for them

refused.refuses: text density, OCR volume, or 'looks like a document photo' as a sensitivity signal
refused.why: the same discipline P5 applies to screenshots: dense text describes receipts, whiteboards, and book pages alike. Sensitivity rules key on named labels and shapes, never on volume.

refused.refuses: consuming P5's UnauthorizedTranscription as a detector input
refused.why: the dispatch prompt lists it beside the P5 signals, but live code (src/extractors/long_tail.py) makes it an exception that propagates — a contract violation about the CALL, not stored evidence about the file. Nothing is persisted for a rule to cite, so a rule keyed on it would have empty evidence_refs by construction. Recorded here so the divergence from the prompt is deliberate and visible.

refused.refuses: currency symbols or amount columns as finance-protection evidence
refused.why: receipts, price lists, budgets and homework all carry amounts; 00 routes isolated transactional documents to the Receipts and Confirmations residual, not to protection.

uncertain.question: Does 'detects and protects them before any cloud or automated placement decision is allowed' protect EVERY file that activates a safety schema (every receipt that legitimately activates finance), or only the protectable core the detector rules name?
uncertain.both_sides: Broad: the sentence says 'Finance ... material', not 'some finance material', and over-protection is user-revisable. Narrow: protecting every receipt makes hybrid mode nearly useless for the finance-adjacent bulk of a real corpus, and 00's residual library expects isolated receipts to be placeable. The saf-* rules above implement BROAD until Joseph rules; also raised as the NJ-2 seam (protect-then-extract vs extract-under-protection).

uncertain.question: The section-8.4 corpus list names 'employment materials' and 'educational records'; no rule above protects either. Should they get proposed kinds?
uncertain.both_sides: For: they sit in the same corpus sentence as identity documents. Against: coursework and recruiting are the product's launch domains — protecting them wholesale would gate the exact material the product exists to organize, and 00 lists them as things the corpus 'can include', not things that 'enter a protected state'. Left unauthored; transcripts remain catchable by user reclassification and (where they carry national-ID values) by det-id-national-id-labeled.

uncertain.question: Should an archive whose MANIFEST names protected-looking members (passport.jpg inside submission.zip) classify the archive?
uncertain.both_sides: For: section 2.5 makes manifest names real evidence, and an application packet archive plausibly holds an ID. Against: a manifest name is a filename, and filename-only inference is refused above; the archive's contents were never read, so evidence_refs would cite names only. Left unauthored — the conservative outcome is that an uninspectable archive resolves unreadable_unclassified, which the gate already denies.

uncertain.question: Every label list above is English. Localized biodata, tax, medical and notary wordings are absent.
uncertain.both_sides: Same position as catalogue 04's localized screenshots and 07's localized document names: easy to add, impossible to choose correctly without knowing the corpus languages. The OCR language ratification (English + CJK + Western European) says which languages will produce TEXT; the labels for those languages need a decision, likely folded into R5's jurisdiction work.

uncertain.question: Messaging-app chat exports (.txt WhatsApp exports, Telegram JSON) are private correspondence with no email source_type and no P5 signal rows.
uncertain.both_sides: A timestamp-prefixed-line pattern could catch WhatsApp exports, but the same shape matches server logs and lab notebooks. No honest conjunction found without a corpus; recorded so the gap is visible rather than discovered later.

uncertain.question: min_value_bearing_labels draws the completed-vs-blank line, but a form with one field filled (a name on an otherwise blank W-9-shaped form) sits on the line.
uncertain.both_sides: Protect-on-one-value is the safe direction (a name on a tax form is already personal data); requiring more reduces noise. This is exactly why the count is an injected slot: the value is Joseph's or the deployment's, never this file's.
